what: When the section’s bottom edge touches the bottom of the screen, pin the section and push the inner strip left by the overflow width, 1:1 with scroll distance (scrub, no curve). The pushed distance is exported as the element’s --fx-pin-shift (px) so the frame and vertical strip move by the same amount during the pin. On phones (750px or less) it stays vertical.

options.from: Minimum width (px) at which it pushes sideways, default 751 — 0 means it pushes sideways even on phones (the strip is not unrolled vertically)
options.[data-fx-part=track]: Sliding strip (child inside window) — width: max-content
options.start: Pin start (ScrollTrigger start), default ‹100% bottom› (when the section’s bottom edge touches the bottom of the screen). brand uses ‹top top›
options.scrub: scrub value (seconds) — if given, it lags behind the scroll by that much, default true (immediate). brand is 1
options.end: Pinned distance — by default 1:1 with the scroll distance, track means strip width − window height (Brand A: the section is stretched by the strip width and pinned with sticky) · width means the strip width as is (Brand B) · <n>With w, n times the window width (original offsetWidth × n — ki-e-to 1.5w)
options.shift: if inset, the pushed distance is ”strip width − screen width + window left margin × 2” — the right of the last cell keeps the same margin as the left (Brand). Default is the width overflowing the window · step is the first [data-fx-part=step] width × (number of steps − 1) (when the original pushes by blocks[0].offsetWidth × (n − 1) — Brand)
options.sm: At or below this width (px), sm-end and sm-scrub are used — for cases where the original sets a fixed distance and follow-along separately on phones. Default 0 (no split)
options.narrow: fade: from the layer below: instead of unrolling vertically, sections stay pinned and are layered over each other [data-fx-part=step] changes in turn — over screen height × slide count (scrub fade-scrub, default .3), when progress reaches the next slide’s share only that slide turns on with fade-dur (default .5s) and fade-ease (default power2.out) (Brand mobile Approach section). Positioning that stacks the steps is the using side’s CSS.
options.fade-start: narrow: fixed start of fade, default top top

note: While pinned, the original adds is-pinned to html and moves the vertical strip at the page edge down by the same amount with translate. The consumer only needs to apply --fx-pin-shift to that strip.
